newsitem.title: USA: Harcourt completes National Education tender.
newsitem.headline: Harcourt completes National Education tender.

text.p: Harcourt General Inc. said Thursday it has successfully completed its tender offer for all shares of National Education Corp. at $21 per share in cash.
About 34.6 million, or 96 percent, of National Education's 36 million outstanding shares tendered in the offer, which expired Wednesday.
Harcourt, based in Chestnut Hill, Mass., said it would begin payment for the accepted shares promptly.

National Education, a leading provider of off-site professional training, will give Harcourt another distribution channel for its educational books. Harcourt's $811.6 million offer surpassed a rival $750 million bid by Sylvan Learning Systems Inc., a Baltimore, Md.-based operator of learning centres for children.
National Education's stock was unchanged at $20.875, while Harcourt edged down 25 cents to $46.75 early on the New York Stock Exchange.

Harcourt said National Education will be merged with a subsidiary of Harcourt General and each National Education share not previously purchased in the tender offer will be converted into the right to receive $21 in cash.
The merger is expected to be completed by June 10.

Harcourt also said that with its acquisition of the National Education shares, it has acquired control of Steck-Vaughn Publishing Corp. National Education owns about 83 percent of Steck-Vaughn's common stock.

"With the successful completion of our tender offer for NEC, we can now devote our energies to integrating these businesses and building our presence in the fast-growing educational services market," said Richard Smith, chairman and chief executive of Harcourt General.
